scope: D3D9/RenderWare device and platform boundaries: device and context creation, backbuffer and render targets, presentation, render and material state, texture and mesh upload, viewport and transform state, lighting, and Win32 frame/runtime calls. Gameplay-facing Cell presentation callers are named only where they configure or submit these seams; no third-party implementation reconstruction.

boundaries.gameplay_caller: Application renderer initialization and resize paths; no direct gameplay caller was found for the D3D wrapper itself
boundaries.original_callee: Graphics::RenderUtils::CreateDevice and SetPresentationParameters; inside the statically linked RenderWare D3D9 target they invoke IDirect3D9::CheckAdapterFormat and IDirect3D9::CreateDevice
parameters: adapter format and selected output configuration
state_changed: device-owned state and main color/depth render targets
device-ready flag set to 2 after successful subsystem initialization
boundaries.lifetime: Process/application lifetime; rebuilt on renderer resize and lost-device recovery paths.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Adapter-format checking, device creation, render-target creation, and the subsequent graphics subsystem chain must succeed; failure aborts initialization and reaches the existing Direct X unavailable failure path.
boundaries.timing_order: Resolve resolution and presentation mode, create/check the D3D device, create color/depth targets, bind the main color target, initialize render-state/sampler/shader subsystems, then publish the ready flag and timing stamp.
boundaries.openspore_concept: IRenderer lifecycle and resize, with a host-owned surface/swapchain and explicit main color/depth attachments.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IGpuDevice::createDevice, configurePresentation, resize, and destroy; return typed backend errors instead of exposing D3D interfaces or wrapper globals.

boundaries.boundary: Backbuffer, main render targets, and presentation attachment
boundaries.gameplay_caller: RenderWare terrain and model frame passes; gameplay code observes the resulting image but does not own the D3D surface or swapchain
boundaries.original_callee: RenderWare device-target calls corresponding to IDirect3DDevice9::GetBackBuffer, SetRenderTarget, and the later Present operation; the exact static RW function is not SDK-named
parameters: main color render target and depth target handles
structures: IDirect3DDevice9-compatible surface state behind the RenderWare wrapper
boundaries.lifetime: Attachments follow the device; swapchain or backbuffer state follows the window size and presentation mode.
boundaries.failure_semantics: A missing or invalid target prevents the render pass; present/device-lost failures require the same recreate/resize path as device creation. Exact HRESULT-to-gameplay error propagation is not runtime-observed.
boundaries.timing_order: Acquire or select the backbuffer, bind color and depth targets, record the frame, finish/submit rendering, then present; resize waits for prior work before replacing targets.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Swapchain render pass and main color/depth attachments, separate from gameplay scene and world handles.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IGpuDevice::beginPresentFrame, setRenderTargets, endPresentFrame, present, and resizePresent; expose a presentable surface contract rather than D3D pointers.

boundaries.boundary: Statically linked RenderWare D3D9 runtime and dead D3DX import boundary
boundaries.gameplay_caller: No direct gameplay caller; the static RenderWare D3D9 target is called by renderer and draw infrastructure
boundaries.original_callee: Raw IDirect3D9 and IDirect3DDevice9 vtable methods inside RenderWare; d3dx9_27.dll is imported but has no observed call sites
parameters: D3D device, context, and resource pointers
D3D9 state, texture, buffer, render-target, and presentation arguments
state_changed: raw D3D device state and resources behind the RenderWare wrapper
D3D texture, stream, index, render-target, and lighting state
boundaries.lifetime: Static RenderWare code and device resources live for the application/device lifetime; D3DX import lifetime is irrelevant because no call site is observed.
boundaries.failure_semantics: D3D HRESULT failures propagate through RenderWare subsystem initialization or draw/present paths; the original implementation does not define gameplay-level failure semantics.
boundaries.timing_order: D3D calls are issued only when RenderWare initializes device resources, binds draw state, submits a frame, or presents it; gameplay does not call raw D3D interfaces.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Backend-specific GPU implementation hidden behind the renderer and platform adapters.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: Replace D3D9 and dead D3DX imports with a Vulkan/SDL/GL adapter; keep only draw-state order, resource lifetime, and error categories at the compatibility seam.

boundaries.boundary: Active shader, material, texture-slot, and render-state cache
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell presentation configuration and RenderWare terrain/model draw submission
boundaries.original_callee: Graphics::ActiveState::SetTexture and SetShaderData; RenderWare::CompiledState::SetRaster/GetRaster; MaterialShader lookup and the RenderWare device-target state calls
outputs: backend draw state ready for mesh submission
state_changed: vertex declaration and D3D9 sampler/render state behind the wrapper
boundaries.lifetime: Material/shader identities are cacheable for renderer lifetime; texture bindings and shader constants are frame or draw state and may be rebound when changed.
boundaries.failure_semantics: A missing shader/material or texture binding leaves the draw invalid or uses a prior/default state according to the RenderWare implementation; exact error presentation is not gameplay-observed.
boundaries.timing_order: Select/preload material and raster, update shader constants and texture slots, set the vertex declaration, then bind streams and issue the indexed draw.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Material and texture bindings are presentation state, not gameplay object identity; keep stable material IDs and slot semantics while changing the backend representation.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IMaterialBindings plus an on-change render-state cache, with descriptor/pipeline bindings and typed material constants.

boundaries.notes: The cache and binding order are compatibility-relevant. D3D9 sampler modes, shader bytecode containers, and RenderWare object graphs are replaceable implementation details.

boundaries.boundary: Vertex-stream, index-buffer, and indexed mesh submission
boundaries.gameplay_caller: RenderWare mesh, terrain-quad, and model-world draw passes
boundaries.original_callee: RenderWare::Mesh::SetIndexBuffer, SetVertexBuffer, SetIndicesCount, and Render; underlying D3D9 SetStreamSource, SetIndices, and DrawIndexedPrimitive calls occur inside the static RenderWare device target
parameters: vertex buffer, offset, and stride per stream
structures: IDirect3DDevice9 draw state behind the wrapper
boundaries.lifetime: Vertex/index buffers are asset/device resources; the cached bindings are frame or draw state.
boundaries.failure_semantics: The index-scope check can suppress a stale index binding; a missing declaration, buffer, or unsupported draw state prevents or invalidates the draw. The original caller does not convert this into a gameplay-level error.
boundaries.timing_order: Read the active shader declaration, rebind only changed streams, unbind surplus streams, bind indices when changed and in scope, then issue DrawIndexedPrimitive.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Mesh topology, index count, vertex layout, and draw ordering are the minimum gameplay-facing rendering contract.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IMeshDraw with bindVertexStream, bindIndexBuffer, setPrimitive, drawIndexed, and explicit unbinding; map to Vulkan vertex/index buffers and pipeline state.
boundaries.notes: This is intentionally limited to stream/index state and draw ordering. It does not reconstruct the full RenderWare mesh, skeleton, blend-shape, or model implementation.

boundaries.boundary: Texture and raster upload into GPU state
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Cell GFX preload/display and terrain/model texture selection; gameplay selects texture identity, not the D3D texture object
boundaries.original_callee: Graphics::ITextureManager and ActiveState texture binding; RenderWare raster creation/extraction/fill paths feeding the static D3D9 device target
parameters: width, height, format, and mip chain
outputs: texture bound to a material slot
state_changed: GPU texture resource and mip chain
structures: D3D9 texture/sampler state behind the wrapper
boundaries.lifetime: Raster and texture resources follow asset/device lifetime; slot bindings are frame or draw state.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Invalid or unsupported raster data, allocation failure, or upload failure prevents texture availability; no gameplay semantic is assigned to the backend error beyond content not being drawable.
boundaries.timing_order: Decode or load the raster, allocate and upload mip data, register the texture, select the material raster, and bind the slot before draw submission.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Keep on-disk raster/DXT5 semantics and stable texture identity while replacing upload with a backend texture adapter.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: ITextureUpload and ITextureManager with createTexture, uploadMip, bindTexture, and clearTexture operations.

boundaries.gameplay_caller: Renderer frame setup and terrain/model draw passes
boundaries.original_callee: Graphics::GlobalState::SetTransform and RenderWare device-target viewport/transform operations; the exact SDK anchor for a distinct viewport setter is not established
outputs: configured coordinate transform for subsequent draws
boundaries.lifetime: Viewport follows the current render target and resize; transforms are per-camera, per-world, or per-draw state.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Invalid dimensions or unavailable camera/view state can invalidate the frame; the original implementation does not expose a gameplay-level error for this infrastructure state.
boundaries.timing_order: Select render target and dimensions, set viewport and projection, update camera/world transforms, then submit meshes.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Camera and view values are gameplay inputs; D3D transform and viewport state is renderer state behind them.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: setViewport, setViewProjection, setWorldTransform, and setRenderTarget on IGpuDevice or a render-pass state object.

boundaries.lifetime: World and layer handles follow the Cell presentation lifecycle; lighting and shadow resources follow renderer/device and world lifetime.
boundaries.failure_semantics: Missing lighting or world services prevent a complete presentation state; the original failure is presentation/infrastructure failure and is not a demonstrated gameplay transition.
boundaries.timing_order: Create or bind Cell worlds, preload resources, initialize lighting/shadow/effects state, start display, then render the active worlds.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Cell world/layer identity and display ordering are gameplay-facing presentation data; D3D light records and RenderWare world objects remain backend details.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IPresentationWorld and ILightingState with createWorld, setLayerVisibility, startDisplay, setLights, and shadow/effect toggles.

boundaries.notes: The Cell world and display sequencing is gameplay-adjacent and named; the D3D lighting implementation is not. Keep the world/layer handles and visibility contract, not D3D9 light or RenderWare world layouts.

boundaries.boundary: Win32 window, event pump, and frame timing runtime
boundaries.gameplay_caller: Application/Canvas frame loop and simulator update; the gameplay layer consumes ordered events and frame deltas but does not call Win32 directly
boundaries.original_callee: PeekMessageW, TranslateMessage, DispatchMessageW, InvalidateRect, GetDC, CreateWindowExA/W, QueryPerformanceCounter, QueryPerformanceFrequency, and related USER32/KERNEL32 imports
parameters: window client dimensions or device context
state_changed: Win32 message queue and window invalidation state
boundaries.lifetime: Window and message pump live for the process; timing samples and frame state are per frame; the QPC device stamp is recorded during renderer initialization.
boundaries.failure_semantics: WM_QUIT terminates the pump; failed window/device-context creation follows the platform failure path. Timing calls are expected to provide monotonic samples, but exact error handling is not gameplay-observed.
boundaries.timing_order: Poll and dispatch platform events, update host/window state, obtain frame timing, execute the application/mode update, render, and then invalidate or present according to the host loop.
boundaries.openspore_concept: Gameplay needs normalized event ordering, monotonic time, frame identity, and window dimensions; it does not need Win32 message IDs or QPC implementation details.
boundaries.modern_abstraction: IPlatformHost::pollEvents, monotonicNow, frameDelta, windowSize, and requestQuit, backed by SDL or another host runtime.

boundaries.notes: This boundary is platform compatibility, not a reconstruction of Win32 or CRT. The message pump is explicitly identified in the recon report, but no positive Cell-mode runtime trace is available.

unresolved: The frozen triage export contains no direct D3D or IDirect3D9 SDK-named function; raw D3D9 vtable dispatch remains inside statically linked RenderWare and is not independently enumerated.
No separately named SDK anchor was established for SetViewport or Present; preserve only target dimensions, transform ordering, and presentation ordering.
D3D9 fixed-function lighting, sampler modes, texture memory layout, and shader bytecode remain visual-semantic compatibility targets rather than reconstructed platform code.
No positive runtime trace or pixel oracle currently verifies device init, resize/lost-device recovery, swapchain presentation, lighting, or the final frame ordering in the original binary.
